title: Forks
intro: One piece attacks two at once. Your opponent can only save one of them.

lessons.title: Knight forks
lessons.summary: The knight's jump makes it the best forker.

steps.text: A fork is a move that attacks two pieces at once. Watch the knight jump to c7.
The knight attacks the king and the rook. The king must move out of check, and then the rook is lost. Forks with check are the strongest.
Find the knight fork of king and queen.
steps.hint: Look for a square a knight's jump away from both g8 and d7.
steps.ifWrong: Find the square that attacks both the king and the queen.
steps.ifRight: Check and attack on the queen: she is lost.

steps.text: One knight jump wins the game. Find it.
steps.hint: Which square is a knight's jump from both g8 and e8? No black pawn guards it.
steps.ifWrong: Look for a knight check that also attacks the queen.
steps.ifRight: Check and fork: the king moves, and the queen falls.

lessons.title: Every piece can fork
lessons.summary: Queens, pawns and the rest attack two targets too.

steps.text: Any piece can attack two things at once. The queen is great at it, attacking in eight directions. Even a little pawn can fork two big pieces.
Give check with the queen and attack the rook at the same time.
steps.hint: Find a square on a diagonal to g8 that also lines up with a2.
steps.ifWrong: Look for a check that also hits the rook.
steps.ifRight: Check, and the rook is next.

steps.text: Fork two pieces with a pawn.
steps.hint: A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally in front of it.
steps.ifWrong: Push a pawn so it attacks both black pieces.
steps.ifRight: A pawn fork. One of the pieces is lost, and the d4 pawn protects e5.
